잠언 27:1.content: Boast not thyself of to morrow; for thou knowest not what a day may bring forth.

잠언 27:2.content: Let another man praise thee, and not thine own mouth; a stranger, and not thine own lips.

잠언 27:3.content: A stone is heavy, and the sand weighty; but a fool’s wrath is heavier than them both.

잠언 27:4.content: Wrath is cruel, and anger is outrageous; but who is able to stand before envy?

잠언 27:5.content: Open rebuke is better than secret love.

잠언 27:6.content: Faithful are the wounds of a friend; but the kisses of an enemy are deceitful.

잠언 27:7.content: The full soul loatheth an honeycomb; but to the hungry soul every bitter thing is sweet.

잠언 27:8.content: As a bird that wandereth from her nest, so is a man that wandereth from his place.

잠언 27:9.content: Ointment and perfume rejoice the heart: so doth the sweetness of a man’s friend by hearty counsel.

잠언 27:10.content: Thine own friend, and thy father’s friend, forsake not; neither go into thy brother’s house in the day of thy calamity: for better is a neighbour that is near than a brother far off.

잠언 27:11.content: My son, be wise, and make my heart glad, that I may answer him that reproacheth me.

잠언 27:12.content: A prudent man foreseeth the evil, and hideth himself; but the simple pass on, and are punished.

잠언 27:13.content: Take his garment that is surety for a stranger, and take a pledge of him for a strange woman.

잠언 27:14.content: He that blesseth his friend with a loud voice, rising early in the morning, it shall be counted a curse to him.

잠언 27:15.content: A continual dropping in a very rainy day and a contentious woman are alike.

잠언 27:16.content: Whosoever hideth her hideth the wind, and the ointment of his right hand, which bewrayeth itself.

잠언 27:17.content: Iron sharpeneth iron; so a man sharpeneth the countenance of his friend.

잠언 27:18.content: Whoso keepeth the fig tree shall eat the fruit thereof: so he that waiteth on his master shall be honoured.

잠언 27:19.content: As in water face answereth to face, so the heart of man to man.

잠언 27:20.content: Hell and destruction are never full; so the eyes of man are never satisfied.

잠언 27:21.content: As the fining pot for silver, and the furnace for gold; so is a man to his praise.

잠언 27:22.content: Though thou shouldest bray a fool in a mortar among wheat with a pestle, yet will not his foolishness depart from him.

잠언 27:23.content: Be thou diligent to know the state of thy flocks, and look well to thy herds.

잠언 27:24.content: For riches are not for ever: and doth the crown endure to every generation?

잠언 27:25.content: The hay appeareth, and the tender grass sheweth itself, and herbs of the mountains are gathered.

잠언 27:26.content: The lambs are for thy clothing, and the goats are the price of the field.

잠언 27:27.content: And thou shalt have goats’ milk enough for thy food, for the food of thy household, and for the maintenance for thy maidens.
